title: Reasoning Ontology
abstract: This document specifies how CHOIR's computational primitives are organised §1 : a three-layer architecture L0 Meta / L1 Core / L2 Domain with dependencies pointing upward only, a four-way entity hierarchy, seven relationship families with explicitly declared algebraic properties, two separate inheritance systems, a namespace and versioning scheme, and nine validation checks the ontology must pass against itself §2–§8, summarised at §11 . The ontology being designed is an ontology of reasoning, not of any subject matter — it contains no grahas, no statutes, no diagnoses; those live in domain layers that attach to it §1, §6 . The source carries the status "Draft for review": it is drafted but not accepted as specification , and per MANIFESTO.md — as the source itself states at §8 — the ontology is a hypothesis and needs its own acceptance tests.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.html: This document specifies how CHOIR's computational primitives are organised (§1): a three-layer architecture (L0 Meta / L1 Core / L2 Domain) with dependencies pointing upward only, a four-way entity hierarchy, seven relationship families with explicitly declared algebraic properties, two separate inheritance systems, a namespace and versioning scheme, and nine validation checks the ontology must pass against itself (§2–§8, summarised at §11). The ontology being designed is an ontology of reasoning, not of any subject matter — it contains no grahas, no statutes, no diagnoses; those live in domain layers that attach to it (§1, §6). The source carries the status "Draft for review": it is drafted but not accepted as specification, and per MANIFESTO.md — as the source itself states at §8 — the ontology is a hypothesis and needs its own acceptance tests.

sections.heading: Research Question
sections.html:
The source states its own framing at §1: computational_primitives.md established which primitives exist and why; this document specifies how they are organised — "the class hierarchy, the relationship hierarchy, how properties and rules inherit, how domain layers attach without contaminating the core, how names are scoped, and how the whole thing changes over time without breaking anything that depends on it" (§1).

The document declares its dependency on computational_primitives.md, and declares that it feeds knowledge_graph_spec.md, choir_intermediate_representation.md, and domain_independence.md. It records the reserved DAALE boundaries it touches as daale/ontology/base.py and relationships.py (front matter).

sections.heading: Finding
sections.html:
Three layers, dependencies upward only

The ontology is stratified into three layers with a strict dependency direction: nothing at a lower number may reference anything at a higher number (§2).

LayerContainsChange policy (as stated)
L0 · METAPrimitive kinds, admission criteria, the type system — what kinds of thing can exist"Changes: almost never. Requires constitutional review."
L1 · COREDomain-independent reasoning: Entity, Rule, Evidence, Exception, Conflict, Context…"Changes: rarely, versioned, supersession only."
L2 · DOMAINSubject-matter vocabulary: jyotisha:Graha · law:Statute · med:Diagnosis"Changes: freely, independently per domain."

The source characterises this as "the domain-independence claim made structural" (§2): if a Jyotiṣa requirement forces a change at L1, either the change is genuinely universal — and must be justified in all five reference domains — or the design has leaked. It notes that domain_independence.md §6 turns this into a measurable acceptance criterion, namely that the number of L1 edits required to onboard a new domain should be zero (§2).

§2.1 tabulates what may live at each layer. Subject nouns (Graha, Statute, Drug) are forbidden at L0 and L1 and defined only at L2. Precedence orderings and confidence weights are marked forbidden at L1 and defined at L2; derived-fact computation (kernels) is marked interface only at L1, with the implementation at L2. The precedence machinery and the confidence structure are defined at L1. The source identifies the last four rows of that table as "the ones that leak in practice" and states the governing pattern: L1 owns the mechanism, L2 owns the parameters (§2.1). Its worked instances of the pattern: conflict resolution machinery is universal, but the fact that a mūla text outranks a ṭīkā is a Jyotiṣa fact; confidence aggregation is universal, but the weight assigned to scholarly consensus is domain-calibrated (§2.1).

Entity hierarchy: a four-way split

The top-level split follows §2 of computational_primitives.md — the reasoning-about / reasoning-with axis (§3). Under CHOIRObject (L0, everything addressable) sit four branches:

  • Referent — things reasoned ABOUT: Entity (identity-bearing, with Agent, PhysicalEntity, AbstractEntity, SituationalEntity), Occurrent (Event, Process, Phase), and Quality (Attribute, State, Measure).
  • Proposition — things that can be true: Condition (evaluated to select), Assertion (claimed to hold), Constraint (enforced to reject), the last subdividing into IntegrityConstraint, ApplicabilityConstraint, and NormativeConstraint (violable by design).
  • ReasoningArtefact — things reasoned WITH: Rule, Exception (with RebuttingDefeater, UndercuttingDefeater, PremiseDefeater), Inference, Evidence, Conflict, Resolution, Proposal, Decision.
  • MetaObject — things ABOUT the reasoning: Context, Provenance, ConfidenceRecord, Trace, and Source (with Text, Locus, Edition, Author, Tradition).

§3.1 records three placements as contested rather than settled:

  • Process and Phase are admitted at L1 but "were not in the 001 primitive set." They are admitted as defined terms (composites) because daśā systems, litigation stages, disease courses and project phases all instantiate them identically — the source calls this "a strong C3 signal even though they fail C2" (§3.1).
  • Measure carries a scale_type field (nominal / ordinal / interval / ratio), because the scale type determines which operations are legal. Ṣaḍbala strength units, GRADE recommendation levels and credit ratings are ordinal, and the source states that averaging ordinals is a category error that "appears constantly in scoring systems"; the ontology's contribution is to make the error detectable (§3.1).
  • SituationalEntity "remains the open question flagged in 001 §6.1." It is retained as a sub-kind rather than dissolved into Entity + part-of + Context on fidelity grounds — a bhāva, a legal office and an anatomical site are treated by their corpora as things with their own significations, not merely as positions. The source records this explicitly as "contested, not resolved" (§3.1).

Relationships are first-class, and must declare their algebra

Because relationships are first-class objects (001 §3.6), they carry their own hierarchy and metadata schema (§4). Seven families: StructuralRelation, PositionalRelation, TemporalRelation (Allen's 13), EpistemicRelation, NormativeRelation, InfluenceRelation (marked second-order), and CausalRelation.

Every relationship type must declare arity, transitivity, symmetry, reflexivity, and inverse; the source states plainly that "None are assumed" (§4.1). The declared table covers subclass-of, part-of, instance-of, occupies, aspects, supports, contradicts, derives-from, strengthens, and produces. The table records contradicts as symmetric with itself as inverse, strengthens with arity "2 (target may be an edge)", and produces with arity n. The source notes that instance-of being non-transitive while subclass-of is transitive "is the classic punning trap; it is declared explicitly to keep reasoners from composing them" (§4.1).

§4.2 states a consequence for storage: InfluenceRelation and UndercuttingDefeater may target a relationship instance, not just an object. This is given as "the structural reason CHOIR cannot use plain RDF triples as its storage model without reification — see knowledge_graph_spec.md §2" (§4.2). The illustration used is Exaltation(Guru, Karka) strengthening the edge Guru ──occupies──▶ Karka.

Two inheritance systems, kept separate

The source states that keeping property inheritance and rule inheritance separate "prevents most of the pathologies that afflict large ontologies" (§5).

Property inheritance (§5.1). Identity-defining properties (identity criterion, primitive kind) and structural properties (arity, algebraic properties of relations) use strict single inheritance and override is forbidden. Defeasible properties (typical values, default significations) inherit multiply via role mixins and may be overridden with a record. Annotational properties (labels, comments) inherit multiply and override freely.

Strict single inheritance for identity is justified as eliminating the diamond problem "where it would actually hurt." Role-like multiple membership is expressed with mixins carrying only defeasible properties: a graha that is both a natural malefic and a functional benefic for a given ascendant "is not a multiple-inheritance conflict; it is one entity with two context-scoped defeasible property sets" (§5.1).

Every override is recorded as an object, not silently applied:

Override ::= ⟨ subject, property, inherited_value, override_value,
               context, justification, source ⟩

The source states that this "is what makes exceptional significations explainable rather than mysterious. An un-recorded override is a specification bug" (§5.1).

Rule inheritance (§5.2). For a rule R scoped to class C, with D a subclass of C:

  1. Applicability inherits downward — R applies to instances of D.
  2. Specificity inverts priority — a rule scoped to D outranks a rule scoped to C on lex specialis grounds; the child wins. The source identifies this as utsarga/apavāda, "the same principle Pāṇini encodes in his paribhāṣā apparatus and that legal systems encode as generalia specialibus non derogant."
  3. Conclusions do not merge — two applicable rules produce two Inference objects, both recorded; adjudication happens later in the conflict phase, "never during matching." execution_pipeline.md §4 is cited as making the saturate-then-adjudicate ordering mandatory.
  4. Exceptions inherit, and may be excepted — an exception attached to R applies to D's instances unless a D-scoped exception-to-the-exception overrides it.

The source volunteers that point 3 "is the design decision most likely to be questioned, since it is more expensive than resolving during matching," and defends it on the ground that precedence can depend on the full set of fired rules: a rule may win by lex specialis against one competitor and lose by source authority against another, "and neither judgement is available mid-match" (§5.2).

Deliberate absence (§5.3). There is no default-value inheritance for states. States are time-indexed observations, and inheriting them from a class "would fabricate observations." Only attributes and defeasible significations inherit.

The extension contract for domain layers

§6.1 states the contract as two explicit lists. A domain layer may define new subject classes under Entity, Occurrent, Quality; define new relationship subtypes under an existing L1 family; supply precedence orderings, source-authority rankings, and confidence weights; register derived-fact kernels against the L1 kernel interface; and declare context dimensions beyond the six core ones.

A domain layer may not add a new top-level branch to the entity hierarchy; add a new relationship family; change the arity, metadata schema, or algebraic declarations of an L1 relation; alter conflict, confidence, or explanation machinery; or introduce a new primitive kind.

The escalation path is stated rather than left implicit: "If a domain cannot be expressed within these bounds, that is a finding about the core ontology, and it is escalated as a constitutional change under §7.3 — not patched locally" (§6.1).

Derived-fact kernels (§6.2) are the one place domains legitimately need arbitrary computation — the source's examples are "which house is Jupiter in, counted from the Moon", "is this filing within the limitation period", and "is this dose above the renal-adjusted maximum". These are isolated behind a narrow L1 interface:

Kernel ::= ⟨ name, input_types, output_type, context_requirements,
             determinism_guarantee, provenance ⟩

Kernels must be deterministic and side-effect free, because the traceability invariant (001 §3.16) requires re-derivation to reproduce identical results; a kernel consulting the wall clock or a mutable external source "breaks replay and is rejected." Kernel outputs enter the graph as ordinary State objects with provenance naming the kernel and its version, so a conclusion depending on an ephemeris computation can be traced to which ephemeris (§6.2).

Namespaces, identity, and versioning

Namespaces (§7.1). choir:meta/… (L0), choir:core/… (L1), choir:jyotisha/…, choir:law/us-federal/… (sub-scoped by jurisdiction), choir:med/… (L2). Identifiers are stable and opaque; display labels are separate and may be multilingual — choir:jyotisha/graha/Guru never changes even if the preferred English label does. A Sanskrit term gets one canonical identifier in IAST transliteration, with Devanāgarī, SLP1 and vernacular labels attached as annotations. Homonyms are namespaced apart, never merged: choir:jyotisha/Guru (the planet) and choir:jyotisha/social/Guru (the teacher) are distinct identifiers, and symbol resolution between them "is a compiler task with recorded justification, not an ontology shortcut" — see shloka_compiler.md §5.

Two identity schemes (§7.2). Nominal identifiers (choir:core/Evidence) apply to ontology classes, relations, and contexts and are stable, human-readable, and curated. Content addresses (sha256:… of canonical form) apply to rules, inferences, and evidence instances and are immutable, deduplicating, and forgery-evident. The source draws out one consequence: "two texts that state the same rule produce the same rule hash", so they unify into one rule with two provenance records — "exactly the 'independent attestation' signal the evidence model needs (evidence_model.md §4.3)". Obtaining this from the identity scheme rather than from a matching heuristic is described as "a significant simplification" (§7.2).

Versioning (§7.3). Semantic versioning per namespace, with declared change classes:

ChangeVersion bumpAllowed at
Add a class or relation subtypeMINORL1, L2
Add an optional propertyMINORL1, L2
Deprecate (retain, mark)MINORL1, L2
Tighten a constraintMAJORL1 with review, L2 free
Change an identity criterionMAJORL0/L1 constitutional review only
Remove anythingMAJORConstitutional review only

The governing rule is supersession, never mutation: an ontology object is immutable once published, a change creates a new version and a supersedes edge, and "any conclusion ever drawn under version n remains re-derivable under version n forever." The source states the reason: "it is the only way to answer 'was this decision correct at the time', which is the question every audit actually asks" (§7.3). The deprecation lifecycle is active → deprecated (with replacement) → retired (no new references); nothing is deleted.

Compatibility contract (§7.4). Because DAALE modules will attach to these definitions, the source states the contract explicitly: a dependent pinned to choir:core@1.x will not break on any MINOR release; MAJOR releases publish a migration note listing affected identifiers and their replacements; content-addressed objects never break, because "the hash is the version."

The ontology's own acceptance tests

§8 opens by stating that "The ontology is a hypothesis (per MANIFESTO.md) and needs its own acceptance tests," and records that the files these checks should populate — choir/ontology/primitive_validation.md and relationship_validation.md — are currently empty. Nine checks are specified:

#CheckMethodFails if
V1Every class traces to an admitted primitive or a declared compositeStatic walk of the hierarchyAn orphan class exists
V2No L1 object references an L2 identifierNamespace dependency scanAny upward reference
V3Every relation declares arity + algebraic propertiesSchema completeness checkAny undeclared
V4Every override is recorded as an Override objectDiff inherited vs effective propertiesA silent override
V5Identity criteria are stated positively and negativelyManual review against C1Either half missing
V6Three-domain instantiation for every L1 classPortability matrix (domain_independence.md §6)Fewer than 3
V7Every class has a stated falsifierRegister completenessAny blank
V8Hierarchy is acyclic under subclass-of and part-ofCycle detectionAny cycle
V9No inheritance of State defaultsStatic rule checkAny state default

The source singles out V6: "the expensive one and the one that matters most: it is the ontology's own C3 test, run continuously rather than once" (§8). It does not report results for any of V1–V9 — these are specified checks, not executed ones.

Worked example: one configuration, three domains

§9 instantiates the same L1 structure in three L2 vocabularies with no L1 changes, described as "the domain-independence claim in miniature", with the full treatment deferred to domain_independence.md.

L1 structureJyotiṣaLawMedicine
EntityGuru (graha)Lessee (party)Patient
EntityKarka (rāśi)Leased premisesRenal system
PositionalRelation: occupiesGuru occupies KarkaLessee occupies premises—
StateGuru is exaltedLease is in defaulteGFR is 28
AttributeGuru is a natural beneficInstrument is a leasePatient's blood type
ConditionGuru in a kendra from CandraDefault continuing > 30 dayseGFR < 30
RuleGajakesarī yoga arisesRight of re-entry accruesReduce dose
Exception (undercutting)Nīca-bhaṅga cancelsWaiver by acceptance of rentDialysis in progress
InfluenceRelationAspect strengthens the yogaMitigation reduces reliefComorbidity worsens prognosis
ContextRāśi chart, natal, Parāśara schoolJurisdiction, court levelGuideline version, care setting
SourceBPHS, ch./v., editionStatute §Guideline §, grade

The source draws attention to the Exception row: all three are undercutting, not rebutting. "Waiver does not mean 'the opposite of re-entry'; nīca-bhaṅga does not mean 'the inverse of the yoga's results'; dialysis does not mean 'increase the dose.'" The typology from 001 §3.12 "earns its place identically across all three" (§9). Note that the occupies row has no Medicine instantiation — the cell is empty in the source.

Status of this document

The source is headed "Status: Draft for review" and belongs to Phase 1 — Computational Foundations. It is drafted but not accepted as specification. The document-level statement is made by choir/research/README.md, which records that all 18 deliverables are drafted, none accepted, and that "Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md"; MANIFESTO.md itself states the underlying formulation as "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth." The source makes the same claim of the ontology at §8. The acceptance tests V1–V9 that would test this one are specified but their target files are recorded as empty.

sections.heading: Architectural Implications
sections.html:
For CHOIR's storage layer. §4.2 states that because InfluenceRelation and UndercuttingDefeater may target a relationship instance rather than an object, CHOIR "cannot use plain RDF triples as its storage model without reification," and points at knowledge_graph_spec.md §2. The summary (§11) restates this as the ontology forcing "the storage decision in 003."

For the execution pipeline. Rule inheritance point 3 — conclusions never merge during matching — is stated as requiring execution_pipeline.md §4 to make the saturate-then-adjudicate ordering mandatory (§5.2). Adjudication cannot happen at match time because precedence depends on the full set of fired rules.

For the evidence model. Content addressing of rule instances yields independent attestation detection without a matching heuristic: two texts stating the same rule produce the same hash and unify into one rule with two provenance records, which is the signal evidence_model.md §4.3 needs (§7.2).

For the compiler. Homonym resolution (e.g. choir:jyotisha/Guru vs choir:jyotisha/social/Guru) is assigned to the compiler as a task with recorded justification rather than being handled by merging identifiers in the ontology — see shloka_compiler.md §5 (§7.1).

For domain independence as a measurable claim. §2 states that the layer discipline is the domain-independence claim made structural, and that domain_independence.md §6 converts it into an acceptance criterion: zero L1 edits to onboard a new domain. V6 (three-domain instantiation for every L1 class) is designated the ontology's own C3 test, "run continuously rather than once" (§8).

For DAALE. The source records the reserved DAALE boundaries it touches as daale/ontology/base.py and relationships.py (front matter), and §10 flags daale/ontology/decision.py as the boundary affected by the unresolved question of whether Decision belongs at L1 at all. §7.4 states the compatibility contract explicitly "Because DAALE modules will attach to these definitions": MINOR releases are non-breaking for a dependent pinned to choir:core@1.x, MAJOR releases must publish a migration note listing affected identifiers and their replacements, and content-addressed objects never break.

For audit. Supersession-never-mutation is justified in the source not as storage fastidiousness but as the only way to answer whether a decision was correct at the time (§7.3).

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.html:
The source records five open questions at §10, verbatim in substance:

  1. SituationalEntity — genuine sub-kind, or Entity + part-of + Context? Carried forward from 001 §6.1, "still unresolved."
  2. Are Process and Phase needed at L1, or should daśā / litigation-stage structures be L2 patterns over Event + part-of? "Retained provisionally on C3 grounds."
  3. Context dimension extensibility. Permitting L2 to add context dimensions (§6.1) risks domains inventing incomparable lattices, "which would break cross-domain conflict resolution. May need a registration discipline."
  4. Mixin conflict. Two defeasible mixins supplying contradictory defaults currently resolve by context specificity. "Whether that is always right is untested."
  5. Should Decision be L1 at all? It may be an institutional-process notion rather than a reasoning notion. Relevant to the reserved daale/ontology/decision.py boundary.

Further items the source records as unfinished or unverified elsewhere in the text:

  • choir/ontology/primitive_validation.md and relationship_validation.md are stated to be currently empty (§8); the nine validation checks V1–V9 are specified but no results are reported for them.
  • Process and Phase are admitted at L1 despite failing C2, on a C3 signal alone (§3.1).
  • The rule-inheritance decision that conclusions do not merge during matching is self-identified as "the design decision most likely to be questioned" and as more expensive than the alternative (§5.2).
